newsitem.title: USA: FedEx to launch Internet order/delivery service.
newsitem.headline: FedEx to launch Internet order/delivery service.

text.p: Federal Express Corp. said Wednesday it will soon offer a computer software package that will allow companies to use the Internet to buy and sell goods that would then be delivered by the courier company.

The company said that businesses using its new BusinessLink service would be able to build their own "sites" in its central computer and promote their goods to other businesses on the World Wide Web portion of the Internet, the global computer network that is rapidly becoming an important medium for many businesses.
The Memphis-based delivery company said the new service, which is available now to selected customers, will be available nationally early next year.

It said the service will offer a complete range of integrated information, transportation and logistics services, including order entry and confirmation, inventory management, transportation, invoicing and after-sales service for returns or repairs.

"FedEx BusinessLink solves one of the key limitations of electronic commerce by linking the automated order and fulfilment system to the delivery of the product to the end customer," Laurie A. Tucker, a senior vice president of Federal Express, said in a statement.
"With FedEx BusinessLink, a company of any size can become a global marketer and create new sales channels without the need to invest in additional customer service and warehousing."
FedEx's stock lost 50 cents to $82 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
